mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts, using the current values at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form "X gives K items to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Only adding K to Y's count while leaving X unchanged.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements that equate a signed difference to another difference as (A - B) = (C - D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of C and D" (or similar).
mathgap.example: Treating (A - B) = (C - D) as |A - B| = |C - D|, ignoring the sign.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person (e.g., "X has N items"), set that person's current count to N at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating the given count as a later value, ignoring earlier transfers that affect the person.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all statements into algebraic equations, collect them into a linear system and solve for all unknowns.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After processing all statements and forming the full set of equations.
mathgap.example: Guessing a value without solving the linear system.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; discard any solution that yields a negative or fractional count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the linear system, verify each variable satisfies the integer‑non‑negative constraint.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with -3 items.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For conditional transfers, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds, perform the transfer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement includes a condition like "If X has more than N items, X will transfer...".
mathgap.example: Executing the transfer even when the condition is false.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says persons redistribute items to ensure each has an equal amount (including splitting one person's items equally among others), pool the involved items and divide equally among the recipients, assigning any remainder according to problem constraints (typically zero).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes equal sharing or redistribution of items.
mathgap.example: Leaving the original person with their original count after splitting all their items equally among others.

mathgap.title: Signed interpretation of "difference between" phrase
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions "the difference between the number of X and Y", interpret it as the signed difference X - Y (order matters).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the phrase "difference between" appears in a relational statement.
mathgap.example: Treating "difference between X and Y" as |X - Y| (absolute value) instead of X - Y.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "the number of X increases by N times", multiply X's current count by N (i.e., X = X * N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering "increase by N times" phrasing.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "increases by 2 times" as X = X + 2 instead of X = X * 2.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X - Y = N (i.e., X = Y + N) and "X has N fewer than Y" as X - Y = -N (i.e., X = Y - N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses "more than" or "fewer than" to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Reversing the direction, treating "X has N more than Y" as Y = X + N.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often defaults to interpreting "difference" as magnitude, ignoring sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of terms and treat "difference between X and Y" as X - Y.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Transfers are sometimes processed out of order, leading to incorrect current counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements immediately when they appear, updating both parties before any later statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat a given count as immutable, overlooking later transfers that modify it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as the current value at that point; subsequent transfers can change it.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may forget to subtract the transferred amount from the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing "X gives K to Y", subtract K from X and add K to Y.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in "X has N more than Y" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may misinterpret the comparative phrase and swap the operands.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that "X has N more than Y" means X = Y + N (i.e., X - Y = N).

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat the phrase as an absolute difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "difference between X and Y" as the signed difference X - Y, preserving order.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by N times" as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The wording can be confused with "increase by N" (addition) versus "increase by N times" (multiplication).
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat "increase by N times" as a multiplication: X = X * N.
